opportunities.title: Ledger says 'we weren't hacked'—but if you didn't update, you were exposed
opportunities.why_now: OneKey just reproduced a live transaction-replacement exploit against outdated Ledger Ethereum apps, and Ledger's rebuttal that it was 'already patched' is the real story for anyone who hasn't updated firmware in months.
opportunities.angle: Security explainer: walk through the attack mechanics, why 'patched' doesn't help users who never update, and a checklist to verify your Ledger app version right now.

opportunities.title: $8.7M gone in one price manipulation: how Moonwell's oracle got played on Base
opportunities.why_now: A fresh, quantifiable DeFi exploit (MAMO price manipulation) just hit Moonwell, offering a concrete case study while the wound is still open.
opportunities.angle: Post-mortem breakdown of the oracle/price manipulation vector, contrasted with 'this keeps happening' pattern across lending protocols—end with a checklist for evaluating collateral oracle risk before you deposit.

opportunities.title: Kraken locked users out over sanctioned funds—your compliance exposure isn't hypothetical anymore
opportunities.why_now: Users were briefly frozen after a flood of sanctioned transactions hit Kraken, a real-time demonstration of how OFAC exposure can lock retail accounts with zero warning.
opportunities.angle: Security/compliance piece: explain how sanctioned-address contamination spreads through mixers/exchanges, and practical steps to avoid getting your account frozen (wallet hygiene, screening tools).

opportunities.title: ChatGPT is quietly logging into your accounts—what that means for your seed phrase
opportunities.why_now: OpenAI's agentic ChatGPT signing into accounts without explicit user action is a direct preview of the attack surface AI agents create for anyone storing crypto credentials nearby.
opportunities.angle: Opinion/warning piece connecting agentic AI account access to crypto custody risk—if an agent can sign into your accounts, what happens when one has exchange API keys or a hot wallet extension open?

opportunities.title: The Sandbox will make bridge-hack victims whole—but the bridge model is still the weak link
opportunities.why_now: The Sandbox's $700K bridge exploit and 1:1 repayment pledge is fresh and gives a clean hook to revisit why bridges remain crypto's most-hacked category.
opportunities.angle: Analysis: use the incident as a jumping-off point for a 'bridges are still the soft underbelly' piece, tallying cumulative bridge losses and what reimbursement pledges do (and don't) fix.
